0.reason: the case pins the stamp and path owners, which carry the staleness rule; a sentinel on read_cache_document and write_cache_document would strengthen it but changes no behaviour this node ships

findings.text: The note says the fourteenth case 'fails if any of them restates the stamp, the path, the document read or the write'. The case at tests/test_findings_are_read_from_a_write_time_index.py:415 holds only the stamp and the path, plus the absence of the two _note_findings_index wrappers; nothing replaces read_cache_document or write_cache_document with a sentinel, so findings.py could restate either and the case would stay green. Restating the document read is not harmless: a copy that swallows a different exception set makes one cache rebuild where the other trusts a half-written file, which is the drift the case exists to catch. The claim covers two of the four rules it names.

The importer-population arm was run under '-n 6' (logs/importer-population-base.log and -head.log header commands), while the plan's §14 done-when caps the arm at '-n 4'. The one id the head arm adds, test_overdue_review_duty_reports_age_without_a_dispatch_command, is a wall-clock age assertion that read 'review overdue by 51m 2s' against a '50m' expectation, which is exactly the class the concurrency cap protects. The arm also ran at a1e64678, one production change short of the delivered head 1ebeebce (review_records.forget_cache_code_stamps gained a clear at 14723e72). The serial rerun passes at both arms and the added id is not attributable to the change, so the conclusion stands, but the recorded population is not the arm the measure names.
